findings.title: Double-checked locking missing re-check after acquiring write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets releases the read lock at line 43 and later acquires the write lock at line 48, but after acquiring the write lock it does not re-read entryPointAssetsCache before doing the expensive load. If many goroutines call concurrently when the cache is nil (e.g. the first requests in production), all of them will see nil under RLock, block on Lock, and then sequentially reload the manifest from file/CDN and overwrite the cache. The cache is not single-flight; this can cause a thundering herd of disk/network reads and JSON parsing at startup. Add a second cache check immediately after acquiring the write lock (e.g. if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }) before loading.

findings.title: No test for concurrent access or caching behavior
findings.body: This change modifies only webassets.go and adds synchronization around the global cache, but no test is added that exercises concurrent calls to GetWebAssets (e.g. under -race) or verifies that non-Dev callers reuse the cached value and that concurrent startup loads are handled correctly. A regression test would help confirm the data race is actually fixed and would reveal the duplicate-load issue described above.
